confidence_notes: I based the food and drink prices on two web searches. One found the RBA rate. The other found cost-of-living sites (CityCost, Traveltables, Mylifeelsewhere, Expatistan, GlobalCostData). Those sites gave a cappuccino at about USD 1.47–1.88, a budget meal at USD 5.4–10, a mid-range dinner for two at about USD 36, and a domestic beer at about USD 1.1–1.7. Some of that data is old (Traveltables was last updated in 2023), so I moved the values up a little for prices in 2026 and in tourist areas. A draft beer (chopp) served in a restaurant is priced above the city average. The cocktail price (a caipirinha) and the glass of wine were not searched directly. I estimated both from the local beer price and normal Brazilian restaurant markups, so they are less certain. The accommodation prices come from my general knowledge only. I did not check any booking sites. Foz do Iguaçu has plenty of hostels and mid-range hotels for visitors to the falls, and prices can rise in July because of Brazilian winter school holidays. The RBA rate I used was reported for 18 November 2026. My search summary attributed it to the RBA exchange rates page, but I did not open that page myself to confirm it.
comparable_city_reasoning: I set prices just above regional averages for southern Brazil (Curitiba and other mid-sized cities in Paraná). The extra reflects demand from tourists visiting Iguaçu Falls. I also considered nearby Puerto Iguazú in Argentina as a regional comparison.
